root_cause: The mobile pricing control was visible and present, but Playwright scrollIntoViewIfNeeded waited for element stability and timed out before any pointer click. The instability was in Playwright's auto-scroll actionability phase, not in the pricing runtime itself. A later verifier hardening changed the safe Playwright pointer primitive from locator.click() to page.mouse.click() over explicitly validated element geometry. Historical regressions over-specified callback variable names and locator.click(), causing false failures despite preserving the real-pointer invariant.
prevention_rule: For production browser proofs where sticky/responsive layout can keep a visible element moving, use deterministic DOM scrollIntoView to position the target, then preserve a real Playwright pointer click. Never use force:true or DOM click() to manufacture success. When an interaction primitive changes, update every regression asserting that primitive in the same candidate; search for the old primitive before protected CI. Regression tests must assert semantic interaction invariants rather than callback variable names or one Playwright API: deterministic scroll, computed visibility/geometry, real Playwright pointer input, and explicit prohibition of force:true and DOM click bypass.

invariants: scrollIntoViewIfNeeded is not used for this mobile proof
force:true and DOM click bypass remain forbidden
deterministic scroll assertion is callback-variable agnostic
real pointer proof may use locator.click or page.mouse.click after validated geometry

failed_approaches: A second regression test still required scrollIntoViewIfNeeded(), so changing the production verifier without updating every coupled actionability regression caused BRAIN lane failure. Verifier contract changes require a repository-wide regression dependency check.
Asserting literal `el => el.scrollIntoView` and `lossButton.click()` tied the regression to incidental implementation syntax instead of the real pointer-safety contract.

evidence.current_pointer_contract: deterministic DOM scroll + computed visibility/geometry + real Playwright pointer input; no force:true or DOM click bypass
